proofs.proof_tex:
We use three elementary techniques: elimination of nonnegative masses at a zero aggregate budget, the finite-marginal coupling characterization in \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\), and the full-law projection and lifting result in \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\).

Fix an observed array \(q\) and a reduced feasible point in some branch \(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\).  First suppose \(\delta_D=0\).  The defier-budget constraint in \(\mathrm{def:orientation\text{-}polytope}\), together with \(f_x\geq0\), gives
\[
  0\leq \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}f_x\leq 0.
\]
Because \(\mathcal X\) is finite, every summand vanishes: \(f_x=0\) for all \(x\).  By \(\mathrm{def:diagonal\text{-}residuals}\), all entries of \(r\) and \(s\) are nonnegative and
\[
  \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}r_{xw}=f_x=0,
  \qquad
  \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}s_{xw}=f_x=0.
\]
Thus \(r_{xw}=s_{xw}=0\) for every \((x,w)\).  Substitution in the residual identities yields, entry by entry,
\[
  d_{x0w}=q^1_{x0w},
  \qquad
  d_{x1w}=q^0_{x1w},
\]
and hence
\[
  u_{xw}=q^0_{x0w}-q^1_{x0w},
  \qquad
  v_{xw}=q^1_{x1w}-q^0_{x1w}.
\]
Consequently \(d\), \(u\), \(v\), \(c_x=\sum_wu_{xw}=\sum_wv_{xw}\), and the selected margins \(U_x\) and \(V_x\) are functions of the observable array \(q\).  Feasibility itself supplies the required nonnegativity of the displayed differences.

Now also suppose \(\delta_S=0\).  By \(\mathrm{def:selected\text{-}complier\text{-}margins}\),
\[
  a_x=U_x-h_x,
  \qquad
  b_x=V_x-h_x.
\]
The survivor constraints give \(h_x\leq U_x,V_x\), so \(a_x,b_x\geq0\).  The selection-minority constraint therefore implies
\[
  0\leq \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\min\{a_x,b_x\}
  \leq 0\cdot\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}c_x=0.
\]
Finiteness again implies \(\min\{a_x,b_x\}=0\) in every cell.  Since subtracting the common scalar \(h_x\) commutes with taking the minimum,
\[
  0=\min\{U_x-h_x,V_x-h_x\}
   =\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x,
\]
and therefore
\[
  h_x=\min\{U_x,V_x\}.
\]
The branch minority term is
\[
  o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x.
\]
It can vanish only with \(o_x=1\) when \(U_x<V_x\), only with \(o_x=0\) when \(V_x<U_x\), and with either value when \(U_x=V_x\).  Thus the smaller-margin orientation is observable, up to harmless ties.  Conversely, if there are no defiers and selection is one-sided among compliers in each cell, then \(f_x=0\) and one of \(a_x,b_x\) is zero in every cell.  Choosing \(o_x=1\) when \(a_x=0\) and \(o_x=0\) when \(b_x=0\), with either choice at a tie, makes both aggregate budget constraints equal to zero.  The zero-budget union therefore coincides exactly with no-defier, covariate-dependent one-sided selection, rather than merely being an outer relaxation of it.

The same argument gives an explicit endpoint computation before imposing complete selection.  Define
\[
  \ell_x=
  \max\!\left\{0,h_x-
     \min_{-1\leq k\leq K-1}B_{xk}\right\},
  \qquad
  \overline n_x=
  \min\!\left\{h_x,
     \min_{0\leq k\leq K}G_{xk}\right\}.
\]
At zero budgets, \(u\), \(v\), and \(h\) have just been shown to be fixed by \(q\).  The exact coupling statement \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\) says that the feasible values in cell \(x\) are precisely
\[
  n_x\in[\ell_x,\overline n_x].
\]
Its completion clause and \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\) show that the cellwise choices can be made simultaneously and lifted to a full response law inducing \(q\).  Hence the attainable numerators form the Minkowski sum of these finitely many intervals, namely
\[
  N\in
  \left[\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\ell_x,
        \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\overline n_x\right].
\]
Every point of this interval is attained: this follows inductively from
\([a,b]+[c,d]=[a+c,b+d]\), and lifting then supplies the corresponding full law.  If
\[
  H=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}h_x>0,
\]
the denominator is fixed and positive, so division is valid and \(\mathrm{def:identified\text{-}set}\), \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\), and \(\mathrm{thm:attained\text{-}connected\text{-}endpoints}\) give the sharp equality
\[
  \Theta_I(q;0,0)=[L(q;0,0),U(q;0,0)],
\]
where
\[
  L(q;0,0)=
  \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
    \max\!\left\{0,h_x-min_{-1\leq k\leq K-1}B_{xk}\right\}}
       {\displaystyle H},
\]
and
\[
  U(q;0,0)=
  \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
    \min\!\left\{h_x,\min_{0\leq k\leq K}G_{xk}\right\}}
       {\displaystyle H}.
\]
If instead \(H=0\), nonnegativity forces every \(h_x=0\), and the positive-denominator requirement in \(\mathrm{def:identified\text{-}set}\) labels the target empty; no division is made.

The endpoint formulas require no linear program.  For each cell, one forward or backward pass through the \(K\) outcome levels computes all prefix and suffix sums occurring in the \(K+1\) values of \(B_{xk}\) and the \(K+1\) values of \(G_{xk}\).  Taking their minima, forming \(h_x=\min\{U_x,V_x\}\), and summing the cellwise endpoints therefore use \(O(K)\) arithmetic operations and comparisons per cell, hence \(O(mK)\) operations overall.

Suppose in addition that \(S_0=S_1=1\) almost surely among compliers.  Then, for every \(x\), all complier mass is selected under both treatments, so
\[
  U_x=V_x=h_x=c_x,
  \qquad
  H=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}c_x.
\]
When this common denominator is positive, the preceding formulas are exactly the sharp finite-ordinal strict-benefit interval formed from the two complier outcome margins.  Exactness follows from \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\), and the converse full-law construction follows from \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\); thus this is a sharp bound, not only an outer bound.

For \(K=2\), direct substitution in \(\mathrm{def:ordinal\text{-}threshold\text{-}cuts}\) gives
\[
  B_{x,-1}=U_x,
  \qquad
  B_{x,0}=u_{x1}+v_{x0},
  \qquad
  B_{x,1}=V_x,
\]
and
\[
  G_{x,0}=v_{x1},
  \qquad
  G_{x,1}=u_{x0},
  \qquad
  G_{x,2}=U_x.
\]
Because \(h_x\leq U_x,V_x\), the general cellwise interval simplifies to
\[
  \max\{0,h_x-u_{x1}-v_{x0}\}
  \leq n_x\leq
  \min\{h_x,u_{x0},v_{x1}\},
\]
which is the claimed binary reduction.

Finally, the relation to Dong--Heiler is only an anchor-class relation.  Let \(\mathcal X_+=\{x\in\mathcal X:c_x>0\}\).  Their conditional model imposes treatment monotonicity and, within each retained covariate cell, one of the two weak selection-monotonicity directions among compliers; it treats the conditional first stage and assignment overlap as support restrictions \cite[Assumptions~3.1--3.2 and the discussion following Assumption~3.1]{DongHeiler2026}.  In the present zero-budget class, treatment monotonicity follows from \(f_x=0\), and for \(x\in\mathcal X_+\), positivity of \(p_x\) permits the calculation
\[
  P(D_1\neq D_0\mid X=x)
  =P(C\mid X=x)
  =\frac{c_x}{p_x}>0.
\]
Moreover, \(a_x=0\) is equivalent to \(S_1\geq S_0\) almost surely conditional on \((C,X=x)\), while \(b_x=0\) is equivalent to the opposite inequality.  Thus, after restricting to \(\mathcal X_+\) as required by that conditional-first-stage support convention, the present zero-budget class is the finite-covariate, finite-ordinal subclass of the Dong--Heiler structural model under the common randomization, exclusion, consistency, and overlap restrictions.  Conversely, every law in that finite-ordinal subclass has \(f_x=0\) and, in each retained cell, either \(a_x=0\) or \(b_x=0\); it therefore satisfies both present budgets at \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\).  Cells outside \(\mathcal X_+\) have \(c_x=h_x=n_x=0\) and do not affect \(H\), \(N\), or the endpoint sums.  This proves the converse on the stated subclass and support.  It does not identify the positive-budget class with the Dong--Heiler model: positive \(\delta_D\) permits treatment defiers, and positive \(\delta_S\) permits both opposing selection-response types within a cell.

proposed.statement: If \(\delta_D=\delta_S=0\), the branches reduce to no-defier covariate-dependent one-sided selection. If additionally \(S_0=S_1=1\) almost surely among compliers, then \(H=\sum_xc_x\) and \(\Theta_I\) reduces to the standard sharp ordinal strict-benefit interval obtained from the complier marginal distributions; for \(K=2\), its cellwise numerator inequalities reduce to \(\max\{0,h_x-u_{x1}-v_{x0}\}\le n_x\le\min\{h_x,u_{x0},v_{x1}\}\).
proposed.justification: The exact zero-budget elbow fixes the latent residual margins and survivor mass from observables, supplies a closed-form sharp benchmark, and provides an auditable implementation test.
proposed.gap: Dong--Heiler supplies the no-defier, covariate-dependent one-sided-selection structural anchor for an intensive-margin mean; equivalence here is limited to its finite-ordinal zero-budget subclass and does not cover the positive-budget joint-violation model or this strict-benefit target.
proposed.consumer: The closed-form zero-budget endpoints give Job Corps and Oregon analysts a no-linear-program baseline against which every positive-budget sensitivity chart can be checked.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The reopened proof directly uses the two budget restrictions, the reduced-array definitions, positivity for the conditional-first-stage comparison, and the endpoint definitions; the dependency list must expose that complete proof spine.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under conditional IV restrictions, treatment monotonicity, conditional first-stage support, and a covariate-dependent selection-monotonicity direction among compliers, Dong--Heiler analyze an intensive-margin complier mean; the present zero-budget structural class is equivalent only on the finite-covariate, finite-ordinal subclass after removing zero-first-stage cells.
Expands sharp ordinal-benefit bounds to observational settings and imperfect randomized trials.
Derives uniformly sharp bounds for marginal treatment effects among always-observed individuals in a latent-index treatment model, with tighter bounds under monotone sample selection.
Derives nonparametric average-effect bounds under sample selection and noncompliance.
Derives breakdown frontiers for average effects and the proportion benefiting under two assumption relaxations.
Derives LATE and average-effect bounds under joint relaxations of independence and monotonicity.
Constructs an output-sensitive polyhedral decomposition for sufficient-matrix multiparametric complementarity problems.
Uses lexicographic perturbation to obtain a unique continuous optimizer over nonoverlapping regions.
Its confidence interval procedure for the fraction benefiting is pointwise consistent.
Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated-projection confidence intervals.
Provides uniform asymptotic inference using randomly perturbed linear-program value functions.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The zero-budget proposition now proves the precise finite-ordinal anchor-class equivalence, while the positive-budget model remains only informed by the other comparator results.

prose_updates.tldr: Random assignment can coexist with endogenous receipt and outcomes observed only in a post-treatment selected sample. For the probability of strict ordinal benefit among always-selected treatment compliers, defier and minority-selection budgets generate an exact finite union of linear-size rational threshold-cut polytopes, and every reduced point lifts to a full response law. The sharp scalar set is an attained interval, its pointwise endpoints are computed by finitely many rational linear programs, finite rational two-budget charts and simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage are available, and sparse endpoint laws certify attainment. At the zero-budget elbow, defier residuals vanish, the complier margins and \(h_x=\min\{U_x,V_x\}\) are observable, and both endpoints are computed exactly in \(O(mK)\) operations without a linear program. This elbow matches only the finite-ordinal Dong--Heiler anchor class under its conditional-first-stage support convention; the positive-budget model is distinct. The remaining open question is an output-sensitive chart enumerator complete on degenerate and lower-dimensional strata.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-complier bounds, including Dong--Heiler, impose treatment monotonicity and covariate-dependent one-sided selection, while published ordinal-benefit bounds under imperfect compliance omit the post-treatment-selection principal stratum. Existing two-assumption breakdown frontiers also do not resolve a latent survivor denominator that may approach zero. The exact zero-budget anchor is known structurally, but it does not identify the positive-budget joint-violation target.
project_justification.niche: The model permits treatment defiers and both opposing selection responses, limits them through separate aggregate budgets, and targets a finite-ordinal individual-benefit probability within always-selected compliers. Its zero-budget boundary is pinned down by observable residual margins and a cellwise minimum survivor mass, providing a precise anchor rather than identifying the general sensitivity class with a monotone model.
project_justification.fill: Projection and lifting reduce compatible full laws to orientation-indexed threshold-cut polytopes of \(O(mK)\) extended size. The resulting theorems deliver sharp attained endpoints, sparse certificates, finite rational charts, breakdown labels, and simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage. At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), explicit sums of ordinal cut extrema give both endpoints in \(O(mK)\) operations with no optimization.

prose_updates.related_work: Dong and Heiler (2026) are the closest structural anchor: their conditional IV model excludes treatment defiers, requires a positive conditional first stage and assignment overlap on the retained covariate support, and permits either selection-monotonicity direction among compliers in each covariate cell. The zero-budget law class here is equivalent to the finite-covariate, finite-ordinal subclass on that retained support; cells with zero complier first stage contribute neither numerator nor denominator. Their target is an intensive-margin mean, however, and neither this ordinal strict-benefit target nor the positive-budget class allowing defiers and both selection directions is their model. Their Job Corps and Oregon applications motivate the intended empirical mapping. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) provide the closest sharp finite-response analysis of ordinal benefit under imperfect compliance, but omit post-treatment selection and the always-selected complier denominator. Bartalotti, K\'edagni, and Possebom (2023) study always-observed marginal treatment effects under a latent-index treatment rule and obtain tighter bounds under monotone sample selection; their treatment rule excludes defiers and their tightening excludes the opposing selection responses admitted here. Chen and Flores (2015) study average effects with noncompliance and sample selection under monotonicity and mean-dominance restrictions. Masten and Poirier (2020) motivate conclusion-first two-assumption frontiers, and Picchetti (2026) supplies a defier-share sensitivity coordinate, but neither gives the present survivor-complier ordinal ratio. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones (2009) and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski (2007) motivate adjacency and degeneracy tools for symbolic optimization; they do not establish output-sensitive enumeration for these unperturbed disjunctive rational charts. Huang et al. (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Cho and Russell (2024) motivate constrained and projection inference, whereas the result here is conservative simultaneous projection of a finite-sample multinomial primitive region.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The ordinal-cut characterization, full-law projection and lifting, attained connected endpoints, sparse endpoint laws, finite rational charts, breakdown frontier, simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage, and exact zero-budget reduction are proved. At zero budgets, the structural comparison with Dong--Heiler is confined to the finite-ordinal subclass and to covariate cells retained under their positive conditional-first-stage and assignment-overlap convention; no positive-budget equivalence and no transfer of their mean bounds to the strict-benefit target is claimed. The output-sensitive enumerator remains open because component discovery and duplicate-work charging are unresolved: finite all-bases enumeration may inspect exponentially many rejected, singular, duplicate, or nonoptimal bases. No strongly polynomial algorithm, polynomial bound on the number of orientations or charts, root-\(n\) regular endpoint inference at ties, or empirical reanalysis is claimed.
